stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: An inductor $L$ resists changes in current. Click the switch $K$ to close the circuit. Watch $u_L = L\,\dfrac{di}{dt}$ spike to $E$ then decay as the current $i$ ramps up. Slide $L$ and $R$, complete one full ramp to advance.
stages.concept: Establishment: $i(t) = \dfrac{E}{R}\,(1 - e^{-t/\tau})$ and $u_L(t) = E\,e^{-t/\tau}$, with $\tau = \dfrac{L}{R}$. At $t = \tau$, $u_L$ has decayed to $37\%$ of $E$ — the same $\tau$ that shapes ignition coils, DC motors, and every switching regulator.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Hit the orange crosshair: $u_L$ must equal $V^{*}$ at exactly $t^{*}$. Tune $L$ and $R$ so your live curve passes through the target. Many $(L, R)$ pairs work — success depends on $\tau = L/R$.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: Only the target $u_L(t)$ curve is drawn. Read $\tau^{*}$ from the shape on paper, pick $L$ and $R$, then press RUN to reveal your curve. Match $\tau$ to within $\pm 3\%$.
stages.concept: Reading method: at $t = \tau^{*}$, the curve crosses $0.37\,E$ (since $e^{-1} \approx 0.37$). Estimate $\tau^{*}$ from that crossing, then pick any $(L, R)$ whose ratio equals $\tau^{*}$.

labels.peek_hint: find where the target crosses 0.37·E — that t-value is tau*
labels.tip1: close K, wait for the current to fully establish, then re-open to reset
labels.tip2: adjust L and R so your u_L curve passes through the target crosshair
labels.tip3: read tau* from where the target hits 0.37·E, compute L/R = tau*, then press RUN

1.1: Click K once to close, again to open. u_L is the voltage across the coil.
1.2: The dashed 0.37·E line marks where u_L sits at t = tau. Watch it as you change L or R.
1.3: Full ramp means i reaches 99% of E/R (about 5 tau). u_L should have decayed to near zero by then.

2.1: Compute the target tau*: tau* = -t* / ln(V*/E). Then set L/R ≈ tau*.
2.2: Doubling L and doubling R keeps tau the same — the u_L curve won't change.
2.3: Fine-tune with one slider once you're close; small L changes = small tau changes.

3.1: On the target curve, find the t-value where u_L = 0.37·E — that is tau*.
3.2: Or find where the curve visibly settles near zero (≈ 5 tau*). Divide by 5 for tau*.
3.3: Peek gives a reading method. Set L/R = tau*, then press RUN — do the math on paper first.
